new_statements.rule_in_words: Tama is described (from R. C. Stevenson's field notes) as having lexical and grammatical tone, with three level tones implied; the compilers state explicitly that nothing is known about stress, i.e. no word-stress rule is given. Dimmendaal's modern fieldwork data (2014, and by report 2009) transcribe Tama with High/Low tone plus downstep, consistent with a tone-language analysis; no published stress rule was found.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the Mararit remark (two level tones plus a falling tone, after Lukas) concerns a sister language, not Tama.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical/grammatical tone on citation forms (noun singular/plural pairs); stress explicitly undescribed. Text obtained as verbatim scanned snippets from the archive.org full-text index of a controlled-lending scan; tone diacritics on the cited forms are garbled by scanned.
new_statements.identity_note: T&B 1966 ch. 12 treats the 'Tama Group' (TAMA, SUNGOR, MARARIT); the quoted tone/stress lines labelled TAMA refer to Tama proper (tama1331) from R. C. Stevenson's Darfur-side field notes; the falling-tone remark concerns Mararit (mara1398), and Sungor/Assangori (assa1236-type variety, ISO sjg) is a separate language. Dimmendaal's data are from Sudanese Tama speakers (fieldwork 2002-2004). Not to be confused with Tucanoan Tama (Colombia) or Tima (Katla, Nuba Mountains).
